title: A product is more than its model

sections.skill: Explain why a product's behavior is more than its model

questions.prompt: What are system instructions?

choices.text: Questions the user types into the chat box
Directions the company adds to shape answers
The operating system of your phone
The training data used to build the model

questions.correct_answer: Directions the company adds to shape answers
questions.intro: A general description of language models cannot tell you exactly how a particular product will behave. Products add their own layers: SYSTEM INSTRUCTIONS the company writes (for example, "be brief" or "do not give medical diagnoses"), SAFETY FILTERS, TOOLS such as web search, code running or file reading, SETTINGS, and LIMITS on length or usage. Two products built on similar models can therefore refuse different requests, format answers differently, or have different abilities. To know what a product does, test it on your task and read its documentation.
questions.feedback: Companies write instructions that guide their product.

questions.prompt: Two products use similar models, but one refuses a request the other accepts. What is a likely reason?

sections.skill: Compare a restaurant's kitchen with its menu

questions.prompt: In the comparison, the model is like what?

choices.text: The pizza oven
The house rules
The supplier's ingredients
The portion sizes it serves

questions.correct_answer: The supplier's ingredients
questions.intro: Two restaurants might buy ingredients from the same supplier, yet their meals differ: each has its own RECIPES, its own HOUSE RULES ("no substitutions"), its own EQUIPMENT (one has a pizza oven), and its own PORTION SIZES. Knowing the supplier tells you little about what you will be served. An AI product is similar: the model is like the supplier's ingredients, while the company's instructions, filters, tools and limits are like the recipes, house rules, equipment and portions.
questions.feedback: The model is the shared ingredient.

questions.prompt: A workflow that summarized meeting notes worked last month but now formats answers differently. What is a likely explanation?

choices.text: Your computer's clock is wrong
The workflow was never possible
The meeting notes became illegal to summarize
The product updated its instructions or model

questions.correct_answer: The product updated its instructions or model
questions.intro: Products also change. A company may update instructions, add or remove tools, adjust filters, or switch models, sometimes without obvious notice. A workflow that worked last month can break, and a limit that blocked you may disappear. Version names, release notes and help pages are the best record. When results matter, keep a few test cases and rerun them after updates, and avoid building important processes on an undocumented behavior you happened to notice once.
questions.feedback: Products change over time.
